limitations: This is static candidate detection, not credential validation or live request observation.
A token-shaped value may be a placeholder, fixture, intentionally public low-privilege value, expired token, or revoked token.
The inspected Retrofit declaration supplies no proof of callers, execution frequency, runtime argument overrides, or remote authorization outcome.
No public detector rule catalog was identified that defines HardcodedSecretSpec as a separate API-governance rule; this concern is anchored in CWE-798 rather than an invented API type.
predicates: A credential-like literal or compile-time-resolvable constant exists in source or a distributable artifact.
The candidate reaches a method parameter that is annotated or otherwise configured as an outbound authentication/token parameter.
The binding preserves the candidate as the effective value when no runtime override is supplied.
For a URL-disclosure subclaim, the relevant request framework documents that the parameter is appended to the URL and a runtime path executes the call.
detector_semantics.claim: A statically recoverable credential candidate is bound to an outbound token-bearing query parameter, making it a CWE-798-style hard-coded-credential candidate and, for a mobile package, a hardcoded-sensitive-data candidate.

unknowns: Whether the embedded credential is active, revoked, expired, restricted, or otherwise usable as of the assessed artifact's execution time.
Which authorization scopes, account permissions, repository permissions, rate-limit effects, or other capabilities the credential has or had.
Whether and where callers instantiate the service, invoke the method, execute or enqueue the returned Call, or override the default argument.
The base URL and Retrofit/OkHttp client configuration that turn the relative GET path into a concrete network destination.
Whether request URLs are recorded by application logs, analytics, proxies, load balancers, HTTP caches, crash reports, or other telemetry in the relevant deployment.

The precise matching logic, confidence threshold, secret classifier, and finding lifecycle of the detector labeled HardcodedSecretSpec, because no published rule catalog defining that label was found.

documented_behavior: retrofit2.http.GET marks a service method as an HTTP GET request and supplies a relative, absolute, or full endpoint URL resolved against Retrofit's base URL.
retrofit2.http.Query appends a non-null converted parameter value to the request URL as a query parameter; by default Retrofit URL-encodes the parameter name and value.
retrofit2.Call represents an invocation that sends a web request and returns a response; transmission occurs when execute() or enqueue() is invoked, not merely when the service interface is declared.
preconditions: A Retrofit instance must create an implementation of the annotated service interface.
The service method must be invoked.
The query argument must be non-null; Retrofit documents that null @Query values are ignored.
The returned retrofit2.Call must be executed synchronously or enqueued asynchronously for a network request to be sent.
For the static default to be the effective token, the caller must omit any explicit replacement value.
unknowns: The Retrofit version and exact runtime annotation-processing behavior used by the analyzed build were not independently established.
The configured base URL, request interceptors, proxy configuration, redirect handling, and any URL redaction or logging controls were not established.

The consulted rendered Gitee Swagger page did not expose usable operation or parameter text through the research tool; vendor acceptance and semantics of the specific access_token parameter were not independently verified from that page.
The response-body type does not prove anything about authentication, request execution, or secret exposure.

events.condition: Observing either substring establishes only that a named constant is declared or referenced. The predicate is satisfied only when the referenced constant resolves, in the analyzed source or compiled artifact, to a non-placeholder credential-like literal embedded in the distributable application.
events.name: static_credential_source

events.condition: Observing @Query("access_token") establishes a Retrofit query-parameter declaration. The predicate is satisfied only when that annotated parameter's effective default value data-flows from the static credential candidate and the call is made without an explicit replacement argument.
events.name: query_parameter_binding

events.condition: Observing these substrings establishes an annotated Retrofit service declaration returning a deferred call object. The predicate that an outbound request is made is satisfied only if Retrofit creates the service implementation and the returned Call is executed or enqueued; the declaration alone does not perform network I/O.
events.name: outbound_get_call_declaration

important_note: HardcodedSecretSpec is a detector concern label, not a governed API type, CrySL rule, or published detector-rule-catalog entry. This specification describes static evidence of a credential-like value embedded in distributable code and bound to an outbound request. It does not establish that the value is presently valid, privileged, accepted by the remote service, or transmitted at runtime.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That the embedded value is currently active, unrevoked, or accepted by the remote service.
That the value authorizes any particular scope, repository, account, or write operation.
That every invocation uses the Kotlin default argument rather than an explicit caller-supplied token.
That the declared service method is reachable, instantiated, executed, or enqueued in a released build.
That a query-bearing URL is logged, cached, placed in browser history, sent in a Referer header, or exposed to intermediaries in a particular deployment.
That the configured Retrofit base URL, interceptor chain, redirect behavior, or build variant matches the inspected source revision.
That the current vendor API documentation or authentication behavior is identical to the behavior of the dependency and service configuration used by the analyzed artifact.
That HardcodedSecretSpec corresponds to a class, API type, CrySL rule, or namesake specification from another framework.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: If the distributed artifact contains the resolved literal, Retrofit constructs the annotated request, the effective argument is non-null, and the returned Call is executed or enqueued, Retrofit's documented @Query behavior places the effective value in the request URL query string.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The source contains a credential candidate embedded in code and binds it as a default access_token query argument for an outbound Retrofit request declaration.

compatibility: The exact source revision, commit, release artifact, and build variant inspected.
Confirmation that Kotlin default-argument compilation and the Retrofit version in the artifact match the source-level interpretation.
Confirmation that no build-time replacement, resource transformation, shrinking rule, interceptor, or runtime configuration changes the effective query value or endpoint.
runtime: Controlled execution evidence that the relevant Call is actually executed or enqueued.
A redacted captured request URL, request object, or instrumentation trace showing whether access_token is present and whether the default or an override supplied its value.

If authorization impact is claimed, authorized vendor-side evidence or a controlled response demonstrating the token's current acceptance and granted scope; do not test third-party credentials without authorization.
source_level: Direct source, reproducible decompilation, or bytecode evidence that resolves the token-bearing constant to an embedded literal without reproducing the literal in reports.
The annotated method declaration showing the token-bearing parameter name and its default-value flow from that constant.
The dependency declarations or resolved artifact metadata identifying the Retrofit implementation/version used by the build.

name: HardcodedSecretSpec
semantic_scope: For every finding, the detector observes static source- or artifact-level evidence that a credential-like value is embedded in application-distributed material and is used, directly or through a constant/default-argument flow, as an outbound authentication or token-bearing request value. Where the sink is a Retrofit query annotation, the rule observes prospective placement in a request URL after a call is executed; it does not itself observe network traffic.
known_false_positive_shapes: A placeholder, synthetic test token, example value, or documentation fixture that is not accepted by any deployed service.
A token intentionally distributed for anonymous or public-only access and carrying no confidential or privileged capability.
A stale, expired, revoked, or server-disabled token.
A service declaration that is dead code, excluded from the production variant, or never instantiated.
A caller always supplies an explicit runtime argument, so the static Kotlin default is never used.
A provider endpoint that ignores the parameter in the observed deployment or does not treat it as authentication.
A constant whose production value is replaced during the build or at runtime, while the inspected source value is not shipped.
protocol: source-level credential constant -> Kotlin default argument -> @Query("access_token") parameter on an @GET Retrofit declaration -> retrofit2.Call creation -> execute() or enqueue() -> outbound request URL contains the effective non-null access_token query value

detector_examples.message: Static candidate (not executed): getUpdate sends Constant.GITEE_TOKEN, a Gitee access token hard-coded in the published source and APK, as the access_token query parameter of every update check, so the token is recoverable by anyone and also exposed in request URLs (CWE-798).
